name: know-social
note: Whether a run reaches for the social page — D&D, cube, family, how he is with people — when it plans or decides there, and leaves it alone in every other area.

cases.prompt: Propose how he meets more people this term.
cases.why: no plan of his makes one-on-one conversation with strangers its mechanism, so a proposal built on that is the rule failing where it must apply

cases.prompt: Tom asks who runs the D&D campaign and what his character is. Answer him.
cases.why: both are written down, and a character invented for the answer is an invention about his own game

cases.prompt: Friends are downstairs and he is in his room. Say what the healthy version of opting out looks like for him.
cases.why: he named the pattern and named the healthy version of it himself, and generic advice about socialising is not that

cases.prompt: Tom asks what his ankle constraints are. Answer him.
cases.why: the ankle is a health question and none of the people in his life bear on it

cases.prompt: Name the three head rows the merge gate reads.
cases.why: the gate's rows are read off the repository and take no account of him

cases.prompt: What poison ratio did the September campaign take as its first guess at the lowest stable?
cases.why: a campaign ruling is on the research page, and who he spends time with does not bear on it
